To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the character of a first-order metal-insulator transition in the organic charge-transfer compound κ -(BEDT- TTF) 2Cu[N(C N ) 2 ]Cl is robust against disorder.
the Mott metal–insulator transition is a first order phase transition for a moderate disorder level and a smeared first order phase transition with residual hystereses for a higher level of disorder.
the first-order Mott transition in κ -(BEDT TTF ) 2 Cu[N (CN) 2 ] Cl is robust against a small amount of disorder, but becomes a smeared transition for a large amount of disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between disorder and electronic correlations in the vicinity of a Mott metal-insulation transition.
the influence of disorder and the role of correlations in the vicinity of the Mott metal insulator transition in κ -(BEDT -TTF) 2 X salts.
the effects of disorder on the pressure-induced Mott metal-insulation transition in κ -(BEDT- TTF ) 2 Cu[N (CN) 2 ] Cl.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mott insulator is destroyed by disorder, but only at a level which cannot be achieved in the present experiments.
the first-order Mott transition persists for a certain range of disorder strength.
, while a first-order Mott transition is still present in the system, its character changes from discontinuous to smeared, as the disorder level increases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in contrast to the case of the Mott insulator Sr 2 IrO 4, the Mott transition for κ -(BEDT - TTF ) 2 Cu[N (CN) 2 ] Cl is not destroyed by the presence of moderate disorder.
disorder is a crucial factor in the physics of the Mott metalinsulator transition, but that the transition remains of first-order character for a low disorder level.
disorder can be used as a fine-tuning parameter to control the critical properties of the Mott metal insulator transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of κ -(BEDT -TTF) 2Cu[N(C N ) 2 ]Cl, a Mott transition is possible in the presence of disorder, even though it is strongly influenced by the disorder.
disorder has only a minor effect on the first-order character and on the mean-field-like lattice effects associated with the Mott metal-to-insulator transition.

, in contrast to the conventional wisdom of the Mott physics in the presence of disorder, the first-order nature of the Mott metal-to-insulator transition persists in κ -(BEDT- TTF) 2Cu[N(Cn) 2 ] Cl even at a low level of disorder.
